title: IMPRINTS-CETSA Docetaxel and Paclitaxel in MCF-7 cells, 1h incubation
projectDescription: IMPRINTS-CETSA data acquisition of MCF-7 cells treated with Vehicle (DMSO), Docetaxel or Paclitaxel using TMT 10 plex.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein concentrations were determined in the samples using the DC protein assay (500-0116, BioRad) according to the manufacturer’s protocol and equal amounts of total protein from each condition were used for sample preparation. Samples were dried and resuspended in 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB) buffer (T7408, Sigma) in H2O (LC-MS grade, 115333, Merck), reduced with 5 mM TCEP (77720, Bond-breaker, ThermoFisher Scientific) at 65C for 30 min, followed by alkylation with 15 mM 2-chloroacetamide (CAA) (C0267, Sigma) at 37C in the dark. Digestion of the samples was performed with 1:50 Lys-C (Wako Chemicals Ltd) at 37C for 2 h, followed by 1:50 SOLu-Trypsin (EMS0004, Sigma) at 37C overnight, for QP samples, before LysC addition samples were diluted to 2 M UREA with 100 mM TEAB and before trypsin addition they were diluted to 1 M UREA also in 100 mM TEAB. After digestion efficiency was checked, the peptides were labeled with Isobaric Tandem Mass Tags (TMT)-10plex (90110, ThermoFisher Scientific) or (TMTpro)-16plex (A44522, ThermoFisher Scientific) at 37C for 3 h, followed by checking labeling efficiency (>95% TMT-labelled PSMs). Three biological replicates from the treatment conditions at the same temperature were labeled as a set. The labeled samples from the same TMT set were pooled and the labeling reaction was stopped by adding 10% trifluoroacetic acid (Sigma) to reach pH < 3. Samples were dried in a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator (ThermoFisher Scientific) and desalted using Oasis HLB 1cc (10 mg) extraction cartridges (186000383, Waters) according to manufacturer’s protocol. Offline pre-fractionation of the samples was performed by high pH reverse-phase liquid chromatography using the using a Xbridge Peptide BEH C18, 300 A˚ , 3.5 mm, 2.1 mm 3 250 mm column (#186003610, Waters) The fractions were concatenated and dried using a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator (ThermoFisher Scientific). The digested, labeled, and dried peptide sample fractions were resuspended in 0.1% FA (LC-MS grade, 533002, Merck) in H2O (LC-MS grade, 115333 Merck). Online chromatography was performed using Dionex UltiMate 3000 UPLC system coupled to a Q Exactive mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher Scientific). Each fraction was separated on a 50 cm 3 75 mm (ID) EASY-Spray analytical column (ThermoFisher Scientific) in a gradient of programmed mixture of solvent A (0.1% formic acid in H2O) and solvent B (99.9% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid). MS data were acquired using a top 12 data-dependent acquisition method. Full scan MS spectra were acquired in the range of 375–1500 m/z at a resolution of 60,000 and AGC target of 3e6; Top 12 dd-MS2 60,000 and 3e6 with isolation window at 1.2 m/z.
dataProcessingProtocol: Protein identification was performed by Proteome Discoverer software (ThermoFisher Scientific), using Sequest HT (ThermoFisher Scientific) search engines to search against reviewed human Uniprot databases (downloaded on 13 Jan 2017, including 42105 sequence entries and another downloaded on 23 Jul 2018, including 9606 sequence entries). MS precursor mass tolerance was set at 10 ppm, fragment mass tolerance 0.02 Da, and maximum missed cleavage sites of 2. Dynamic modifications searched for Oxidation (M), Deamidation (NQ), and Acetyl N-terminal protein. Static modifications: Carbamidomethyl (C) and TMT10plex or TMTpro-16plex (K and peptide N terminus). Only the spectrum peaks with signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) > 4 were chosen for searches. The false discovery rate (FDR) was set to 1% at both PSM and protein group levels. Only the unique and razor peptides were used for protein assignment and abundance quantification. Isotopic correction of the reporter ions in each TMT channel was performed according to the product sheet. Only the master proteins in the protein group were used for downstream analysis. For each dataset, the peptide abundances were obtained from Proteome Discoverer software (version 2.4). Every peptide with another modification than a TMT one was removed. Then, every peptide dataset has been treated the same way as the protein dataset according to the same method described in 10.1016/J.CELL.2018.03.065.
